none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

budgets.value:
fun p =>
  ⌈2 ^ 120 * p.m ^ 3⁻¹ * (1 + p.Δ * √p.H / (p.ε * √p.ε)) *
      Real.log (2 + (↑(Module.finrank ℝ p.E) + 1) * p.m * (1 + p.Δ * √p.H / (p.ε * √p.ε)) / p.ρ) ^ 2⌉₊

results.references: - Lesi Chen, Chengchang Liu, Luo Luo, Jingzhao Zhang. [Faster Newton Methods for Convex and Nonconvex Optimization in Gradient Complexity](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.17488v3). 2026 (COLT; author version v3). Complexity: $O(b+b^{1/3}\Delta\sqrt H/\varepsilon^{3/2})$ exact-gradient oracle calls and $O(1+\Delta\sqrt H/(b^{2/3}\varepsilon^{3/2}))$ full-Hessian oracle calls, including initialization and output selection, deterministically achieving $\|\nabla f(x)\|\le\varepsilon$ with NALEN. Here $b\ge1$ is the integer Hessian-refresh period; choose $b=\max\{1,\lfloor\min\{m,(1+\Delta\sqrt H/\varepsilon^{3/2})^{3/2}\}\rfloor\}$.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a twice continuously differentiable function f:E→ℝ. Nonconvex objectives are permitted, with f(x₀)−inf f≤Δ.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Oracle 0 returns the exact gradient together with the function value at the queried point, independently of history and seed.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The exact function value is bundled with the gradient in each oracle-0 call.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Oracle 1 returns the entire exact Hessian as a continuous linear operator. Full-Hessian calls and value–gradient calls have separate fixed budgets.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HessianLipschitzSecondOrder.lean: spec.admissible, oracle 1 equality; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The Hessian is globally H-Lipschitz in operator norm; no global gradient-Lipschitz or Hessian-norm bound is imposed. Public parameters are E, x₀, H>0, Δ≥0, ε>0, m≥1, and 0<ρ<1. The objective is hidden. Parameter m imposes no additional restriction on the objective.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HessianLipschitzSecondOrder.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The returned point x must satisfy ‖∇f(x)‖≤ε.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: Both stationarity conditions must hold jointly with probability at least 1−ρ under the execution law.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: The same returned point must satisfy ⟨v,∇²f(x)v⟩≥−√(Hε)‖v‖² for every v∈E.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Approximate second-order stationarity for unconstrained nonconvex objectives with Lipschitz Hessians and exact derivative oracles is a standard formulation; the budgets separately count gradient and Hessian evaluations.
